svg.text: 1 · Components, and how they talk to each other
which is why answers say so.
The analyse / publish split is the trust boundary. The analyse job runs the repository's own build logic and holds no credential;
the publish job holds the credential and runs none of the repository's code. Collapsing them puts a publish credential on a runner
executing repository-controlled code, which is remote code execution by design.
2 · Ingest — from source code to a searchable index
In the repository · no platform involved
In the worker · one module at a time
The sweep compares chunk and symbol ids against what this run just wrote — never commit shas. Comparing shas is right for a new commit and
silently wrong for the two cases that reindex the same one: a deliberate /v1/admin/reindex, and a crashed run retried. Stale rows carried the
matching sha, survived, and the corpus held two versions of the same code at once.
3 · Query — from a question to an answer that cites its evidence
The ACL filter is a hard predicate in the database query, not a prompt instruction and not a post-filter. Filtering after ranking still leaks result
counts and relative scores for repositories the caller cannot read.
Abstention happens BEFORE the model, never after. Handing a model weak evidence and asking it to decline politely is asking it to do the one thing
it is worst at. When retrieval abstains there is no model call at all.
The threshold is calibrated on cross-encoder scores, which are comparable across queries. Fusion ranks are not — a top RRF score of 0.05 means
nothing in isolation — so when the reranker is down the rule changes shape rather than degrading silently.
The in-repo copy is the half of the exit plan that survives the platform
being switched off. Generated docs land as a pull request, and a human
Every tenant table carries org_id and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.
Policies test org_id = kna_current_org(), a per-transaction
setting. A SUPERUSER connection makes all of it SILENTLY inert —
policies still exist, the invariant check still passes, and every
tenant reads every other tenant's source.
assertRlsEffective() runs at startup in every service and refuses
Reads that happen BEFORE a tenant is known need a narrow probe:
authorised by HMAC, not by identity
withRepoProbe git remote -> repo, for webhooks
Anything reading AFTER a principal exists uses withOrgContext.
1 minimise only what a question needs leaves the repo
2 scan fail closed on a finding, before publish
3 classify sensitivity tier per chunk, restricted never embedded
4 ACL in SQL the caller's permissions as a query predicate
5 injection retrieved content wrapped as untrusted data
6 audit every read recorded by chunk id, breadth monitored
A dashed border means optional or not yet running.
Red text is a failure this design exists to prevent.
